What the source says: Hand-typed schedule carries misspellings (CARRLES, VENTILATON, GREEM)
What we did: Corrected whole tokens only, on the name segment
Why / basis: Each settled against a sibling room that spells it correctly - never guessed. Names reach users through rdfs:label_en.

What the source says: Run-together words (REST_ROOMMEN, ABLUTIONMEN, INDIVISTUDY)
What we did: Restored the separator only; wording unchanged
Why / basis: Every sibling room writes the two tokens apart. No abbreviation was expanded.

What the source says: INDIVI probably means INDIVIDUAL; ITT sits in the room-number segment
What we did: Left as-is
Why / basis: Expanding an abbreviation is a rewrite, not a correction; ITT may be a drawing code and a join key. Client's call.

What the source says: Register tags may contain errors
What we did: Left completely untouched
Why / basis: Asset tags are the BMS join key. Only room names were corrected.

What the source says: IO list gives '%' on 20 of its 24 .kW tags, against a description reading 'Power'
What we did: Overrode to unit:KiloW
Why / basis: A power sensor cannot read a percentage. Dar Cairo uses unit:KiloW on all 559 of its Electric_Power_Sensor points.

What the source says: IO list gives 'm/s' (a velocity) on Supply_/Return_Air_Flow_Sensor
What we did: Overrode to unit:L-PER-SEC
Why / basis: Dar Cairo uses L-PER-SEC on all 51 air-flow sensors, SSC on all 118; unit:M-PER-SEC occurs 0 times in either model, and no point in the IO list is named 'velocity'.

Entity / Scope: 30 analog rows in the Selected sheet
What the source says: Humidity and temperature units transposed (AvgSpcHumd as degC, AvgSpcTemp as %rH)
What we did: Took units from the IO list instead
Why / basis: The IO list has both right. The Selected sheet is not used as the unit authority anywhere.

What the source says: Dar Cairo uses unit:PERCENT on this class
What we did: Used unit:PERCENT_RH
Why / basis: Dar Cairo contradicts itself - its Return_ and Supply_Air_Humidity_Sensor both use PERCENT_RH. SSC and the IO list agree with PERCENT_RH.

What the source says: SSC uses unit:RPM on this class
What we did: Used unit:PERCENT
Why / basis: SSC's are Motor_Speed_Fbk (shaft RPM); QNL's are fan VFD SpeedFbk in % of max. Dar Cairo's Speed_Command is PERCENT on all 88.

What the source says: Dar Cairo uses unit:UNITLESS on this class
What we did: Used unit:L-PER-SEC
Why / basis: A flow is not dimensionless - Dar Cairo's value is a missing unit, not a convention. Its own specific flow classes all use L-PER-SEC.

What the source says: Dar Cairo is mixed: UNITLESS x28, PERCENT x1
What we did: Used unit:PERCENT
Why / basis: Dar Cairo's unitless ones read as binary open/close. Its Speed_Command is PERCENT on all 88 and Damper_Position_Sensor PERCENT on all 74.

What the source says: brick:Chilled_Water_Supply/Return_Temperature_Sensor are deprecated in Brick 1.4
What we did: Kept the deprecated Dar Cairo class; recorded the replacement in the ledger note
Why / basis: Client directed - the class is the established join key. Each raises an expected W-TYP-4 naming the entering/leaving replacement.

What the source says: SSC types its own _TripAlm points as the bare brick:Alarm
What we did: Coined para:Trip_Alarm (subClassOf brick:Alarm), defined in row 3
Why / basis: brick:Alarm is reserved for a literal general/summary alarm; SSC's bare typing makes trips indistinguishable from every other alarm.

What the source says: Named in the Selected points sheet but absent from the asset register - no room, no Fed By
What we did: Modelled both units and their 6 points WITHOUT rec:locatedIn, rec:feeds or rec:isFedBy
Why / basis: Rule 1: model the asset and its datapoints, assert nothing about position. Inventing a location would read as surveyed fact. Raises 2 E-FEED-1 and 2 W-GR-2, accepted here.

What the source says: In the asset register and the historian, but the Selected sheet lists no points for it
What we did: Added the 3 points its 245 siblings carry, taken from the historian
Why / basis: Rule 1: points exist in the historian, so they are modelled. The family's own selected signature decides which, so the unit matches its siblings. Its other 5 historian points are not selected on any sibling either.

Entity / Scope: 12 equipment families (AHU, FCU, DX, HEX, pumps, CCU, EF, generator, pressurisation, climate)
What the source says: Manufacturer datasheets give properties per component (cooling coil, fans, motors, outdoor unit)
What we did: Added the 16 metadata predicates in the Dar Cairo/SSC/HQ row shapes: literals as props, quantities as <blanknode> value+unit; component properties on brick:hasPart sub-entities (CHW-Coil, SF, RF, Motor, OD) - all Brick 1.4 classes, no para: minted
Why / basis: The three reference models attach component metadata to sub-entities and write quantities as blanknodes

What the source says: QF HQ v0.4 carries several wrong brick:hasUnit (air flow as unit:V, cooling capacity as unit:HZ)
What we did: Took brick:value and brick:hasUnit from the workbook's 'Value (Dar Cairo)' / 'Unit (QUDT)' columns, never HQ's
Why / basis: Dar Cairo is the unit authority; HQ's own README documents its units as wrong

What the source says: Datasheets tag them PHX/B/01-05, CHWP/B/01-04, 'GENERATOR SET'; the ontology has HEX01-05, CHW_P01-04, ELEC_Gen
What we did: Joined HEX by index (PHX/B/0n -> HEX0n, user-confirmed), pumps CHWP/B/0n -> CHW_P0n, generator -> ELEC_Gen
Why / basis: Prefixes differ but the units correspond 1:1 by number/position

What the source says: FCU datasheets are 28 Euroclima selection sheets keyed by position (B/03,04; 1F/04-54), one model per group
What we did: Expanded each selection-sheet tag to the FCUs it names and wrote its model/capacity/flow/power to every unit in the group
Why / basis: The selection sheet groups identical units under one model; the group tag names them explicitly

Entity / Scope: FCU 2F 06-33; closed control units; climate & pressurisation units; out-of-range CAV/VAV/EF
What the source says: Their datasheet tags do not correspond to any ontology entity (2F numbers 06-33 vs 034-062; CC/B vs CCU_808n; no MCG/PU entity; units absent from the register)
What we did: Left them without metadata and reported every tag in QNL_metadata_join_report.csv; did not guess a join
Why / basis: User confirmed FCU 2F 06-33 are different units, not a numbering offset; the rest have no matching entity - do not assume metadata a source cannot place

What the source says: Points were named as BMS tokens (AvgSpcHumd_PV, RunSts); equipment/rooms used '_' between word-parts
What we did: Aligned to Dar Cairo: datapoints renamed to dashed English from label or class (Return-Temperature, Run-Status); equipment/part tags kept their industry codes (AHU, SF, CHW-Coil) with '_'->'-' within the tag; 277 room name-words dashed. ref:hasTimeseriesId/para:hasEntityId untouched; crosswalk written
Why / basis: Client asked to match Dar Cairo's naming convention; camelCase 71%->0%, join keys preserved via the crosswalk

What the source says: The BAS valve schedule (BAS_QNL_Assets.pdf) gives each unit's CHW control-valve model, FCU actuator model and design flow
What we did: Added a brick:Cooling_Valve part to every FCU/AHU/HEX with rec:modelNumber (FCU valves+actuators Honeywell; AHU/HEX valves ITQ, make not stated); FCU actuator as a para:Valve_Actuator sub-part; gap-filled para:ratedChilledWaterFlowrate on the 43 FCUs that had none (all of 2F 034-062, 1F 059-065)
Why / basis: The BAS is a valid as-built source; brick:Cooling_Valve is Dar Cairo's CHW-valve class (76 uses); para:Valve_Actuator minted (no Brick/Dar Cairo/SSC class for a valve actuator)

What the source says: The BAS valve schedule gives 0.36 L/s where the Euroclima selection sheet gave 0.27 L/s
What we did: Kept the Euroclima value; did not overwrite. Flagged for the supplier. The other 91 of 94 shared FCUs agree within +/-0.02 L/s, verifying the metadata
Why / basis: Two sources, minor disagreement on 3 units; the Euroclima selection sheet is the equipment nameplate, the BAS the valve sizing - a supplier question, not ours to resolve

What the source says: No metering layer existed. A hand-built workbook (VirtualMeters_QNL_manual_v1.xlsm) proposed one from a 9-class x 3-tier matrix.
What we did: Regenerated the layer from that tier matrix against the live ontology rather than importing the workbook, and archived the workbook under projects/QNL/sources/.
Why / basis: None of the workbook's 353 room identifiers matched the live sheet - it was built before align_naming ran. Regenerating makes the identifiers agree by construction instead of by remap.

What the source says: Workbook rooms read QNL_B_001A_BREAK-OUT-AREA; the ontology reads QNL_B-001A_Break-Out-Area.
What we did: Used the ontology form. Zero identifiers changed in the ontology.
Why / basis: A fuzzy key (case, separators, leading zeros) matched 353 of 353, so the two name the same rooms; the ontology form is the one the rest of the sheet and the crosswalk already use.

What the source says: The workbook metered 353 rooms; the ontology has 354.
What we did: Gave it the same four room-tier meters as its siblings.
Why / basis: The room was added by the room-retarget pass (QNL_room_retarget_changes.csv, "new room") after the workbook was built. Note the open question from that pass: if 144 and 145 are one room, 144 should be retired and its meters with it.

What the source says: The workbook gave CHW and HW thermal points unit:KiloW and unit:KiloW-HR, the same tokens as the electrical meters. Dar Cairo splits: brick:Thermal_Power_Meter uses para:KiloWt/para:KiloWt-HR, its own para:CHW_Meter is 70 rows kW against 2 kWt.
What we did: Used para:KiloWt and para:KiloWt-HR, and declared both as qudt:Unit rows.
Why / basis: Client decision. Thermal kW written as unit:KiloW is indistinguishable from electrical kW, so any building rollup that sums demand double-counts. Diverges from the 7 pre-existing QNL thermal rows on unit:KiloW - those are left alone and listed for a later pass.

What the source says: Dar Cairo populates every virtual-meter point with a ref:TimeseriesReference. The QNL historian (QNL_Historian_IO_list_CP2.xlsx) carries no calculated tags at all - zero *_CALC, zero ContributionFraction.
What we did: Wrote the points with no reference row, and listed all 2,920 in QNL_virtual_meter_timeseries_pending.csv with the Dar Cairo tsid proposed and entityId blank.
Why / basis: The workbook wrote 2,912 reference rows with both keys blank. A half-filled blank node looks finished and reads as a working telemetry link; an absent one is visible as W-PT-1 and tracked in a file.

What the source says: Client asked for para:contributionFraction on every unit fed by an AHU, skipping units in shafts or risers.
What we did: Added it to all 297 (246 VAV + 51 CAV) with tsid ContributionFraction and the entityId each unit's existing points already carry.
Why / basis: The shaft rule matched nothing: QNL's shaft-dwelling assets are 62 FCUs and 2 exhaust fans, and no AHU feeds any of them. The rule is implemented for the next building. entity:QNL_CAV-B-S13-050 carries no points, so its entityId was derived - the derivation matches all 296 units that do have one.

What the source says: QNL already carries entity:QNL_Total-Energy typed para:Utility_Meter, with a real historian tag QNL_TotalEnergy.Energy. The tier matrix asks for a building-tier Utility_Meter as well.
What we did: Suppressed the virtual one. A virtual meter only fills a gap where no physical meter exists, and Total-Energy is the physical utility meter.
Why / basis: Client rule, confirmed 2026-09-03: virtual meters are created only for actual meters that do not exist. The generator now carries an ALREADY_METERED list, each entry naming the physical meter that justifies the suppression.

What the source says: 14 pre-existing physical meters (MFM, VCB) share brick:Electrical_Meter with the 360 new virtual ones, so check_consistency compares them as one family.
What we did: Left the class as-is; 25 E-CON errors are accepted and named here.
Why / basis: Dar Cairo does the same - brick:Electrical_Meter covers both its physical and virtual meters. Splitting the virtual ones under a para: subclass would depart from the primary reference to quiet a checker.

What the source says: None carries a brick:meters row. Each is brick:isPartOf entity:Electrical_System with points, and nothing says what it measures.
What we did: Left them as they are; recorded the gap and hand-listed the one suppression it blocked.
Why / basis: The "virtual only where physical does not exist" rule cannot be evaluated from the graph while this holds - it needs a human to say what each meter covers. Adding the brick:meters rows is the durable fix and is proposed in the handover.

What the source says: QNL carries a brick:Building_Chilled_Water_Meter on the main CHW loop with 7 live points, among them CHW-Consumption-KW and CHW-CHW-Energy-PV.
What we did: Kept entity:QNL_CHW-Power-Thermal-Virtual-Meter for now and raised the overlap.
Why / basis: OPEN. By the same rule that removed the Utility virtual meter, this pair looks like a duplicate - the loop meter measures the building's chilled water. Different classes, so no checker will catch it. Needs confirmation that the loop meter covers the whole building.

What the source says: Two MEP drawings schedule the same boxes and disagree on air flow. 1F: 290 l/s on the S11/S15 drawing against 220 l/s on the second 1F drawing. Basement: 261 l/s on the heating-capacity drawing against 251 l/s on the model-and-make drawing. QNL_Full_Metadata.xlsx recorded both and its Open Items sheet marks each "Unresolved".
What we did: Kept 290 l/s and 251 l/s; dropped the other eight rows.
Why / basis: Client decision 2026-09-03, on one rule: where two drawings of the same schedule disagree, keep the one that names the box model, since the flow has to match the box selected. 290 comes with model NBOQOB250 and makes boxes 005-009 one consistent run; 251 comes with model NBOQE03. Title blocks are cropped on every drawing image, so no revision date could settle it instead. Reversible - both values remain in QNL_Full_Metadata.xlsx.

What the source says: Every row declares para:IFC_ID with a blank value; ref:ifcName carries the entity identifier. No reference model carries a real IFC GUID either - across Dar Cairo, SSC, HQ and QNL, none of 2,133 values matches the 22-character IfcGloballyUniqueId shape.
What we did: Filled all 564 para:IFC_ID cells with the entity identifier, the same string ref:ifcName already carried. QF SSC's shape.
Why / basis: Client decision 2026-09-03. SSC writes the identifier into both columns on all 165 of its IFC rows; QNL was already built to that shape but left IFC_ID empty. Note that no delivered model carries a real IFC GUID - across Dar Cairo, SSC, HQ and QNL none of 2,133 values matches the 22-character IfcGloballyUniqueId shape - so para:IFC_ID holds the asset tag, not the BIM GUID that CLAUDE.md describes. If real GUIDs are exported later they overwrite these in one pass.

What the source says: The asset register gives no room for 6 CRACs, 2 DX units, 1 CAV, 1 VAV, 1 booster pump and 15 electrical meters. Earlier practice was to write no rec:locatedIn at all rather than invent one.
What we did: Wrote rec:locatedIn entity:QNL (rec:Building) on all 26. Every one already carried brick:isPartOf its system, so no system row was needed.
Why / basis: PROJECT ASSUMPTION FOR QNL ONLY - not a house rule, and deliberately not written into the skill. An asset with no room is still certainly in the building and certainly on its system, so both are asserted rather than nothing. rec:feeds is still not written - the served space is the part nobody knows. Dar Cairo has precedent, locating 36 entities at a rec:Building. Excludes the 174 parts that also lack a location (137 CHW valves, 22 fans, 10 HEX valves, 2 breakers, 2 pumps): a part inherits its parent's location and Dar Cairo locates only 19 of its 801 parts separately. Clears 26 W-GR-2; the 10 E-FEED-1 stand.
